headline: Leads fell sharply while site traffic rose, and July's small rebound still leaves lead volume well below May's peak.
summary: From May to July, sessions climbed 4,138 to 6,148 (+48.6%) but leads dropped 170 to 114 (−32.9%), and the site-wide conversion rate slipped from 1.88% in June to 1.85% in July even as spend rose 9.7%. More visitors are reaching the site without converting at the same rate, which points at the site or the form rather than the media buy.

findings.title: Traffic up, leads down — opposite directions
findings.detail: Sessions rose 4,138 to 6,148 (+48.6%) from May to Jul 2026 while leads fell 170 to 114 (−32.9%) over the same window. The June-to-July uptick in leads (107 to 114, +6.5%) does not offset the May collapse (170 to 107, −37.1%), so July is still a bad month relative to the window's best month.

findings.title: Conversion rate is drifting down, not recovering
findings.detail: Site-wide conversion rate went from 1.88% in June to 1.85% in July, even with more sessions and more spend. Growing traffic isn't translating into proportionally more inquiries.

findings.title: Paid search cost per lead is high and organic is softening
findings.detail: Paid Search cost per lead sits at $114 in July on $7,519 spend for 66 leads, and Organic Search leads slipped 43 to 41 (−4.7%) from June to July even though paid search leads grew 57 to 66 (+15.8%). The mix is shifting toward the more expensive channel while the free channel weakens.
